hints: A missing subsequence can be built one letter at a time.
For each suffix, know where each DNA letter next occurs.
Choose a letter that minimizes one plus the best answer after its earliest occurrence.
analogy: At each step look for the earliest matching letter in the remaining strand; a missing letter ends the search.
example: For ACGTACGT, AAA is absent, while every two-letter DNA sequence occurs, so length 3 is optimal.
algorithm: Scan the string from right to left while maintaining the next occurrence of A, C, G and T. Let dp[i] be the shortest absent subsequence length in suffix starting at i. For each letter, its candidate is 1 if absent from the suffix, otherwise 1+dp[next occurrence+1]. Store the minimizing letter and next position. Follow these choices from position 0 until choosing a missing letter to reconstruct an answer.
correctness: A sequence beginning with a letter is a subsequence exactly when its remainder is a subsequence after that letter?s earliest occurrence. Therefore each candidate gives the shortest missing sequence with that first letter, and taking the minimum gives the optimal answer.
complexity: For DNA length n, time is O(n) and space O(n).
